# MM-P3-L1-HP01 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01

Scope
- This manual covers planned maintenance tasks and verification steps for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1, model EQ-P3-L1-HP01, located on line P3-L1. Activities include mechanical fastener verification, hydraulic system pressure verification, basic lubrication checks, and documentation practices required before returning the press to production.
- Exclusions: detailed electrical diagnostics beyond visual inspection and logic controller programming changes are not included; consult SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 for electrical and operational procedures respectively.

Background and rationale
- The forging press is a process-critical machine where ram alignment and hydraulic integrity directly affect part quality and operator safety. The main ram bolt secures the ram assembly and transmits forging loads to the frame. Fastener preload influences joint stiffness and fatigue life. The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Adhering to this torque value ensures the fastener achieves the designed clamp load and joint performance.
- Hydraulic system overpressure is a primary hazard for seals, hoses, and valves. The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Maintenance checks verify that safety devices and relief settings maintain system pressure within that limit.
- Reference maintenance and operating standards: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SOP-P3-L1-01, SOP-P3-L1-02.

Tools
- Torque tool suitable for applying and verifying the specified main ram bolt torque. Use a calibrated torque device with traceable calibration certificate. Ensure the torque tool has suitable adapters for the bolt head geometry used on EQ-P3-L1-HP01.
- Pressure measurement equipment compatible with hydraulic systems, rated to exceed the system pressure limit and supplied with calibration documentation. Use fittings and hoses rated for hydraulic fluid and the referenced system pressure limit.
- Hand tools for access panels, retaining hardware, and witness markings. Use non-sparking tools as required by local safety rules.
- Clean cloths, inspection mirror, thickness feeler or shim pack for visual gap assessment, and approved seal repair kit as specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Lockout/tagout materials and personal protective equipment required by SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Coordinate with production and operations using SOP-P3-L1-02 to establish machine downtime and safety perimeter.
  - Apply lockout/tagout in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-01 before any mechanical or hydraulic work. Verify energy isolation visually and by test where applicable.
  - Review MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for component removal and reassembly drawings. Confirm availability of a calibrated torque tool and pressure gauge.
- Mechanical fastener verification and re-torque
  - Remove access covers to expose the main ram bolt and bearing housing. Clean the bolt head and surrounding area to remove scale and lubricant that could affect torque readings.
  - Inspect the bolt, washer, and threads for visible damage, corrosion, or galling. If damage is found, tag the component and consult MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for replacement guidance prior to reassembly.
  - Using the calibrated torque tool, verify the tensile condition of the main ram bolt. The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Apply torque smoothly to avoid shock loads and use the same tool orientation used during calibration.
  - If torque does not achieve the specified reading, remove the bolt, inspect threads, and clean or replace as required per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Reinstall and apply torque to the specified value.
  - Mark witness points on bolt head and adjoining surface to indicate verified torque. Record the torque verification value and torque tool serial number in the maintenance record.
- Hydraulic system verification
  - With mechanical checks complete and covers replaced as required, prepare to verify system pressure. Confirm that hydraulic fluid level and condition meet the criteria in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 before pressurizing.
  - Attach the calibrated pressure measurement equipment to the test port specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Follow safe pressurization steps described in SOP-P3-L1-01.
  - Verify that the system attains normal operating pressure and that pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Monitor relief valve response and look for pressure spikes during a controlled test cycle.
  - If pressure exceeds the system pressure limit, stop testing immediately, isolate the circuit, and follow troubleshooting in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Do not place the machine back into service until the cause is identified and corrected.
- Lubrication and ancillary checks
  - Inspect lubrication points for continuity of supply and accumulation of contamination. Replace worn hoses or fittings per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 guidance.
  - Conduct a short functional test cycle under observation to detect leaks, unusual noise, or movement anomalies. Use SOP-P3-L1-02 for operational sequencing if energized testing is required.
- Completion
  - Restore safety covers and remove lockout/tagout following SOP-P3-L1-01 procedures. Inform operations that the machine is ready for return to service.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical
  - Main ram bolt is installed and verified to the specified main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Witness marking present and legible.
  - No visible damage to bolt threads, housing, or surrounding structure; if present, corrective action documented and replacement parts procured as specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Hydraulic
  - Hydraulic circuit maintains pressure within safe operating limits and does not exceed the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar during controlled verification. Relief valve operation and set points are documented.
  - No active fluid leaks at inspected connections, seals, or hoses during a monitored test cycle.
- Records to keep
  - Maintenance entry documenting tasks performed, parts replaced, and safety steps followed. Include the calibrated torque tool serial number and pressure gauge calibration reference. Cite MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for any parts replaced.
  - Signed completion checklist referencing SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 as applicable, including witness signature from maintenance and production representatives.
  - Photographs of critical areas before and after work where practical, and copies of any nonconformance reports generated during the activity.
- Example entries
  - Example record should include statement of torque verification with the torque value 1425 N·m, the torque tool identifier, pressure verification with reading relative to 330 bar, and a note on any corrective action taken. Maintain records in the document control system as required by local plant policy.

Related documents
- MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1
- SOP-P3-L1-01
- SOP-P3-L1-02
